pr.title: Start a MIDI take where the knobs are: field keys publishes what it sent, and the daemon chases it to the take's first sample (instrument-knobs.md chunk 3)
pr.head: cd59565a363b75945e963f9569091e6f7a3df12f

summary: field keys plays the computer keyboard as a MIDI source named Field Keys, and its knobs, from chunks 1 and 2 of the instrument-knobs plan (#209 and #210 beneath this pull request), turn an instrument by sending MIDI control changes (CCs). field record records a MIDI take through field-audiod, the audio daemon, which opens every MIDI source when it arms and stamps each message with the sample it arrived on.

A take records only the messages that arrive once it has started. So a knob you turned before pressing record, such as juno's cutoff dialed down for a darker pad, played live but rendered at its default in the take. The modulation wheel had the same gap. This pull request, chunk 3, closes it with MIDI alone, in three steps:

1. field keys publishes what it sent. Inside a project, it writes every controller from 0 to 119 it has sent, by channel, to .field/keys.json on each control change, with its own pid, and removes the file when it quits.
  2. field record passes them in arm. When it arms a MIDI take and the publishing process is still running, it adds the list as controllers to the arm request, only for a daemon that lists the new midi-chase feature.
  3. The daemon chases controllers. From the arm, the audio callback keeps the latest value of each controller on each channel: first the seeds arm passed, then every control change that arrives before the take starts, from any source, a count-in included. At the take's first sample it writes one line per controller at at: 0, ahead of every other line, in the order the values last arrived.

The landed notes file needs nothing new: the chased values become ordinary controls rows at at: 0, and the render already applies control changes before note-ons at one instant. With this layer every chunk of the plan is built. Criteria 20 and 21, which need a kitty terminal and ears, are still owed by hand.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• CC. A MIDI control change: a channel, a controller number from 0 to 127, and a value from 0 to 127. A knob in field keys is one CC.
  • Chase. Carrying each controller's latest value into a take that starts later, as a DAW chases controllers when you start playback mid-song.
  • Seed. A controller value field record passes in arm, taken from .field/keys.json; the daemon treats seeds as arriving at the arm.
  • Channel mode messages. CCs 120 to 127, such as All Notes Off. They act once rather than setting a value, so the chase skips them.
  • MIDI primary and companions. With several tracks armed, one take is the primary and the rest are companions on the same clock; a MIDI companion records exactly what the primary hears.

cards.title: Review of this head
cards.html:

groups.title: The arm request carries controllers
groups.kicker: The protocol field, its client, and the daemon's check
intro: arm gains an optional controllers list of {channel, cc, value}, with channel from 1 to 16, cc from 0 to 119, and value from 0 to 127. A daemon that understands it lists midi-chase in hello.features.

The client names the field only when the list is non-empty, and field record fills it only for a daemon with midi-chase, so an older daemon never sees it. The daemon refuses a list that is out of range rather than dropping entries, as it refuses a bad input channel.

files.note: The chasedControllerSchema zod schema, shared by the client and by the reader of .field/keys.json.
armMidi and armTracks take an optional controller list; chase() leaves the field out when the list is empty.
readChaseSeeds validates controllers and converts channels to 0 to 15; arm passes the seeds to armMidi or armSet, and hello lists midi-chase.

checks.text: The list is checked before any arm work, so a bad list returns an error without opening inputs or resetting the chase. Traced by reading dispatch's arm branch.

groups.title: The daemon chases controllers to the take's first sample
groups.kicker: A fixed table in the audio callback, seeded at the arm and written once
intro: The audio callback owns a table of 16 channels by 120 controllers. Each slot holds a value and an order number, the time it last arrived. armSet hands the seeds to the callback under a spin lock that the callback only ever tries, so the callback never blocks; it takes them at the top of a block and starts the table over. Every MIDI message that arrives before the take starts, which the callback used to discard, now goes through chaseArrival instead.

When a take's clock starts, chasePending is set, and stampMidiBlock writes the table's lines at at: 0 just before the take's first stamped message, or at the end of the start block if nothing else arrived. An arrival inside the start block that falls before the start sample is chased first, so the lines are complete and still lead the file. The same push goes to the MIDI primary and every MIDI companion, so each MIDI take of a pass gets the same lines.

checks.text: Every path that drained MIDI before a take's start now chases instead: armed but not recording, a count-in or punch-in still short of its position, and arrivals inside the start block that map before sample 0. Loop takes for MIDI, and loop takes with companions, are still refused, so the loop handoff is untouched.

files.note: ChaseSeed, the new seeds parameters, and the chase's fixed-size members.

checks.text: Open finding: ChaseSeed was inserted between Player's 20-line doc comment and class Player, so that comment now reads as part of ChaseSeed's. Move ChaseSeed above it.

files.note: takeChaseSeeds, chaseArrival, and writeChase, and the calls that replace each discarding drain.

checks.text: The seeds are taken at the top of every block, before any drain, so an arm's seeds always order ahead of the arrivals that follow it. Traced by reading processBlock.
The callback only tries the lock; a failed try leaves the seeds for the next block. arm is refused while recording, so seeds never change under a running take. Traced by reading armSet and record.

The sort runs in place over a fixed array, and the MIDI take's 16,384-message fifo holds a full table of 1,920 lines, so the write neither allocates nor drops lines. Checked by reading MidiCapture in capture.cpp.

Arrivals stamped into a take are not chased. A second record on one arm would start a controller turned during the first take at its older value. field record arms once per take, so nothing does this yet; arming.md chunk 3's lasting arm would.

groups.title: field keys publishes what it has sent
groups.kicker: A session's controllers by channel, written to .field/keys.json
intro: KeysSession already kept each controller's last value by number, for the knob line. It now also keeps them by channel, in the order each value was last sent, and sentControllers() lists those below 120, least recently sent first. That order becomes the seeds' order, so it matches the plan's "in the order their values last arrived".

field keys writes the list to .field/keys.json after each batch of messages that holds a control change, by writing a temporary file and renaming it over the last, so a reader never sees half a file. The file carries the writer's pid. On quit, a field keys removes the file only if its own pid is in it, so it leaves a second session's file alone.

files.note: New: publishControllers, unpublishControllers, and controllersToChase, which ignores the file when its process has exited or the daemon cannot chase.

checks.text: Several field keys in one project publish last-writer-wins, and a crashed one leaves a file whose dead pid makes readers ignore it. The state is tied to a process, not to a daemon connection.

files.note: The sent map, updated in cc(), which every control change goes through, and sentControllers().
send publishes after any batch with a CC, and the session unpublishes at the end.

checks.text: A failed write here throws out of the stdin handler or the turn timer, and nothing catches it, so it ends the session. The review lists catching it as a suggestion.

files.note: Checks the least-recently-sent order and that a panic's CC 123 is left out.

groups.title: field record passes the controllers in arm
groups.kicker: One read of .field/keys.json, just before the arm
intro: When any armed track is MIDI, field record reads .field/keys.json right before it arms and passes the list in either form of arm. An audio-only arm passes nothing. With no field keys running, the list is empty and the daemon still chases hardware controllers from the arm.

files.note: Reads the published controllers and passes them to armTracks and armMidi.

checks.text: A knob turned in the moment between this read and the daemon opening its MIDI inputs reaches neither the seeds nor the chase. The window is one arm round trip, and the plan's design accepts it.

files.note: Tests that controllersToChase reads the file only for a daemon that chases and a running publisher, ignores a corrupt file, and that a quitting session leaves another one's file.
